# Depot

Depot is a local build-artifact service with a Rust CLI and a browser interface. Its four Cargo packages separate domain validation, SQLite/file storage, Axum HTTP delivery and the CLI. Versions are opaque immutable names, with one physical file per version even when checksums match.

## Toolchain and prerequisites

The frozen environment uses Rust/Cargo 1.85.1, Rust edition 2021, system SQLite 3.40.1, Python 3.11, Chromium, Selenium and /usr/bin/chromedriver. Cargo.lock pins the supplied 157 registry packages. SQLite development headers and pkg-config are required; dependencies are never patched. There is no frontend build or Node application service.

For each command inside the project set CARGO_HOME=$PWD/.cargo-home, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target, CARGO_NET_RETRY=0, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3, RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup, RUSTC_WRAPPER= and RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER=. Fetch with timeout 110 cargo fetch --locked. Build each package with timeout 110 cargo build --locked --offline -p PACKAGE, in order depot-domain, depot-store, depot-server, depot-cli. Reuse one mounted Workspace for related Cargo steps. A clean rebuild removes target/ only, retaining the declared dependency source cache; it is not a cold-cache claim.

## Run and configuration

Run DEPOT_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:3000 DEPOT_DATA=depot-data target/debug/depot-server. DEPOT_LISTEN defaults to that loopback address; port 0 selects a random loopback port. Startup prints LISTEN followed by the bound address after catalog reconciliation. DEPOT_DATA is the local catalog/object directory and defaults to depot-data. SIGINT requests graceful HTTP shutdown; close clients first. All tests use bounded requests and process cleanup. Open the printed address in a browser for repository creation, artifact upload with progress, prefix filtering, metadata, downloads and confirmed deletion.

## CLI

The CLI accepts --server URL and --json before or after a subcommand. Responses are structured JSON in both display modes. Commands:

- health
- repo-create NAME --description TEXT
- repo-list --page 1 --page-size 20
- upload REPO NAME VERSION INPUT_PATH
- list REPO --prefix PREFIX --page 1 --page-size 20
- info REPO NAME VERSION
- download REPO NAME VERSION OUTPUT_PATH
- delete REPO NAME VERSION

Example: target/debug/depot-cli --server http://127.0.0.1:3000 --json upload builds widget opaque-v1 fixtures/binary.bin. Inputs may be nested paths; names are independent of input filenames. Upload/download operate in 64 KiB chunks. Downloads write a unique adjacent temporary destination and rename only after completion. HTTP error responses create no partial final destination. Exit codes are 0 success, 2 invocation/identifier/pagination validation, 3 HTTP not-found/conflict and 1 transport/local I/O/unexpected server failure.

## HTTP API

GET /health returns JSON status. POST /api/repos accepts {name,description}, returns 201 and rejects duplicates with 409. GET /api/repos lists repositories sorted by name. GET /api/repos/{repo} returns metadata or 404.

PUT /api/repos/{repo}/artifacts/{name}/{version} streams a raw request body and returns 201 metadata. GET on that identity returns metadata, and GET with /download streams exact bytes with Content-Length, original content type and a quoted SHA256 ETag. Existing identities return 409. DELETE returns 204, or 404 when absent. GET /api/repos/{repo}/artifacts lists ready versions ordered by name then version; prefix filters artifact names.

List parameters are page and pageSize, defaulting to 1 and 20. pageSize ranges from 1 through 100. Lists return {items,page,pageSize,total}; empty lists succeed. Identifiers are 1–64 ASCII letters/digits/dot/underscore/hyphen and begin alphanumeric. Invalid identifiers/pagination return 400; absent resources 404; conflicts 409; storage failures 500. API errors have {error:{code,message}} and do not reveal storage paths. Artifact metadata includes repository, name, version, size, sha256, content_type and Unix-seconds created time. Validated identifiers determine paths below the configured directory.

## Publication, deletion and recovery

The single server owns one SQLite catalog in WAL mode with synchronous=OFF. A unique (repository,name,version) reservation is inserted in uploading state before reading body bytes. Each upload has a unique temporary filename and streams through the hash without whole-object buffering. Completion flushes/closes the file, atomically renames it on the same filesystem, then updates the reservation to ready with size/hash. Only ready catalog rows are visible or downloadable. The reservation ensures concurrent same-identity uploads yield one success and one conflict; different identities may stream concurrently. A reader receives a complete object or 404 when publication/deletion overlaps its open.

Body errors remove the temporary file and reservation. Cancellation or process failure can leave invisible uploading state. At startup, before admitting requests, reconciliation removes object files for all non-ready rows, deletes these rows, and clears leftover temporary upload files. Ready rows and their completed files are preserved. Delete first marks a ready row deleting, removes its own physical file, then deletes the catalog row. A pending deletion finishes at startup. This ordering accepts that SQLite and rename are separate transactions. It proves process restart recovery, with no power-loss durability claim. Back up catalog and object files together only after stopping the server.

Deterministic acceptance hooks: DEPOT_FAULT=after_rename terminates with exit 86 only for an upload version named fault after rename and before ready; DEPOT_FAULT=delete_mark terminates with exit 87 only for deleting version fault-delete after the catalog mark. These are explicit test configurations. Ordinary operation leaves DEPOT_FAULT unset.

## Tests and acceptance

For each package first run timeout 110 cargo test --locked --offline -p PACKAGE --no-run, then timeout 60 cargo test --locked --offline -p PACKAGE. Libraries depot-domain and depot-store support timeout 60 cargo test --locked --offline -p PACKAGE --doc; the two binary-only packages have no doctest target. Run timeout 110 cargo clippy --locked --offline -p PACKAGE --all-targets -- -D warnings per package, and timeout 20 cargo fmt --all -- --check.

Python integration checks run in the Workspace: tests/fixtures.py generates the frozen empty/text/binary/nested/64-small/32-MiB corpus and verifies every frozen hash; tests/registry.py covers validation/pagination/conflicts/concurrency/deletion; tests/recovery.py covers interruption and both restart boundaries; tests/browser.py performs actual Selenium/Chromium interactions and cleans up the driver. tests/full.py core RUN verifies all 68 non-large fixture round trips. Run its stages large-v1, large-identical, large-v2 separately with the same RUN name, committing each step. Each streams and verifies a 33,554,432-byte version. Stage cli verifies all commands and exit codes. Stage remount executes retained binaries and verifies the three large versions after a fresh Workspace mount. RUN must be a new acceptance directory for each complete sequence. Application data, fixture bytes, logs and build output remain inside the project view. Tests leave evidence under test-data/ and acceptance-data/.

## Packaging and limitations

All four packages are intended source distributables. Run timeout 30 cargo package --list --locked --allow-dirty -p PACKAGE for each and inspect source, tests, README and browser asset inclusion. Listings deliberately exclude application data, fixture bytes, Cargo caches and compilation output; package listing does not publish to crates.io or qualify a release. Path dependencies need a matching release process before registry publication.

The service is one trusted local process with no authentication, TLS, quota system, remote database, Cargo registry protocol or application deduplication. Do not expose it to untrusted networks. Physical storage capacity and SQLite/platform format limits apply; uploads have no artificial total-size cap. Recovery covers application process interruption, not a machine failure. Filesystem history does not checkpoint processes, sockets, memory or stdout/stderr. The LayerFS run uses explicit Disposable/WAL/OFF; Durable execution remains disabled by owner. Performance observations in this exercise have unknown cache state and are diagnostics.

import subprocess,os,time,json,urllib.request,signal
p=subprocess.Popen(['target/debug/depot-server'],env={**os.environ,'DEPOT_LISTEN':'127.0.0.1:0'},stdout=subprocess.PIPE,text=True)
try:
 import select
 assert select.select([p.stdout],[],[],10)[0], 'server readiness deadline'
 addr=p.stdout.readline().strip().split()[-1]
 assert json.load(urllib.request.urlopen('http://'+addr+'/health',timeout=5))['status']=='ok'
 r=subprocess.run(['target/debug/depot-cli','--server','http://'+addr,'--json','health'],timeout=10,capture_output=True,text=True)
 assert r.returncode==0,r.stderr
 print(r.stdout)
finally:
 p.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)
 try:p.wait(timeout=5)
 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:p.kill();p.wait(timeout=5)

import subprocess,os,select,signal,json,urllib.request,urllib.error,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import time
root=Path('test-data/m3-'+str(time.time_ns()));root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
p=subprocess.Popen(['target/debug/depot-server'],env={**os.environ,'DEPOT_LISTEN':'127.0.0.1:0','DEPOT_DATA':str(root)},stdout=subprocess.PIPE,text=True)
try:
 assert select.select([p.stdout],[],[],10)[0]
 base='http://'+p.stdout.readline().strip().split()[-1]
 def cli(*args):
  r=subprocess.run(['target/debug/depot-cli','--server',base,'--json',*args],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=15)
  assert r.returncode==0,(args,r.returncode,r.stderr)
  return json.loads(r.stdout)
 cli('repo-create','smoke');cli('repo-list')
 source=root/'source.bin';source.write_bytes(bytes(range(256))*16)
 meta=cli('upload','smoke','binary','opaque.1',str(source));assert meta['sha256']==hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
 assert cli('list','smoke')['total']==1
 assert cli('info','smoke','binary','opaque.1')['size']==4096
 dest=root/'download.bin';cli('download','smoke','binary','opaque.1',str(dest));assert dest.read_bytes()==source.read_bytes()
 print(json.dumps({'m3':'passed','sha256':meta['sha256']}))
finally:
 p.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)
 try:p.wait(timeout=5)
 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:p.kill();p.wait(timeout=5)
